Review the supplied code with seven specialist lenses, reconcile findings, and implement supported fixes using the embedded implementation instructions.

<!-- Generated by scripts/generate-review-skill.py; DO NOT EDIT. -->

**Input**

A local diff, paths, symbols, or feature; optional requirements and delivery baseline supplied by the user.

**Rules**

- This file contains every command instruction needed at runtime. Source paths below are provenance, not files to read or slash commands to invoke. Project code, applicable project rules, and relevant specifications remain inputs.
- Apply only to a request authorizing review and fixes. If the user requests review only, keep all work read-only and omit implementation and its completion gate.
- Resolve one scope before delegation. Use explicit user targets; if none are supplied, use current tracked staged and unstaged changes and state that assumption. If there are none, or the target cannot be resolved locally, ask one focused question and wait. Do not silently review the whole repository or include unrelated untracked files.
- Record the reviewed working-tree state, diff base when applicable, target paths/symbols, relevant requirements, and known delivery constraints. Pass this same context and applicable project rules to every reviewer. Do not invent missing release history, requirements, or compatibility obligations.
- For diff inputs, anchor code findings on changed lines; inspect surrounding code and counterparts as evidence. For paths or features, review their named scope. Identify relevant test files/functions from the scope and pass them explicitly to the test-case reviewer, with the code under test. If no relevant tests exist, record that lens as not applicable; do not invent a missing-test finding from a duplication-only review.
- Run clarity, duplication, hardcoding, redundancy, simplify, test-cases, and value reviews. Do not run review-changes, review-selection, review-pr, review-pr-comment, or review-doc.
- Run one read-only subagent per applicable lens, within available concurrency; queue the rest. Give each worker only its embedded section, the shared scope/context, and the worker contract below. Workers must not delegate or edit. If subagents are unavailable, perform each lens sequentially under the same contract.
- Wait for every reviewer to finish before editing. Retry an incomplete review once when recoverable; otherwise record the coverage gap and continue independent work. Incomplete inspection is never a clean result.
- If the target changes during review, discard affected stale findings and review that scope again before editing. Never overwrite unrelated user changes.
- Reconcile every finding against current code: merge duplicates, verify evidence and proposed replacements, and resolve conflicting recommendations using requirements and behavior. Track each finding as fixed, rejected with a reason, or unresolved. Do not silently discard findings.
- Implement every supported, in-scope recommendation, grouping related fixes into concrete tasks with locations, evidence, desired behavior, preserved contracts, and acceptance checks. A speculative finding or an unresolved requirement/tradeoff is not an implementation task. Ask the user only for decisions necessary to resolve such items; continue independent fixes.
- Use the embedded implement section in the parent, one task at a time. Reviewers remain read-only. The reviewer's no-edits constraint ends at the review boundary and does not prohibit the parent's authorized implementation.
- Implementation tasks use the command's Direct input. Read linked specifications only when actually supplied or relevant; no plan, task document, or implementation companion must be created to begin a sufficient direct fix.
- Validate each fix using applicable checks, then run all applicable lenses against the resulting scope, including the fixes. Allow at most two fix-and-re-review rounds total; report remaining findings or repeated conflicts instead of looping indefinitely.
- Must not commit, amend, push, post comments, create/update PRs, or change requirements or architecture/plan documents. This workflow authorizes local fixes only; "complete" does not mean deployed or merged.
- Before replying: account for every finding and every lens, verify fixed findings against final code, and disclose unresolved decisions, incomplete coverage, and validation limits that affect the result.

**Worker contract**

- Stay read-only: no writes, Git mutations, posted comments, or further delegation. For diff inputs, anchor findings on changed lines; unchanged code and counterparts are supporting evidence only.
- These workflow adaptations replace the embedded commands' user-facing clarification, output, and report-gate behavior. They do not replace review criteria, evidence requirements, read-only constraints, project rules, or permission boundaries.
- Return all findings to the parent in one response, without a summary cap, detail offer, report-approval question, or user interaction. Return missing inputs or conflicting evidence as limitations for the parent to resolve.
- For each finding include lens, verified path/line, concrete problem, evidence, proposed smallest fix, and behavior/requirement consequences. For duplicate tests name both cases and their shared branch and runtime concern; retain distinctions that justify keeping cases.
- Return an explicit clean, findings, not-applicable, or incomplete status, with inspected scope and any limitation. Do not label a partially inspected scope clean.

**Gates**

Command report gates are removed; the implementation Done gate runs once in the parent after the full workflow, not after each fix. If blocked on required input, ask that question instead; do not stack it with Done. Omit Done when no changes were needed or made.

| Step | Prompt | n |
|------|--------|---|
| Done | Happy with implementation? (y/n) | Address scoped feedback, validate, and re-ask |

**Output**

```text
<Implemented | Partially implemented | Blocked | No changes needed>: <concrete result.>
<Unresolved findings, decisions, rejected recommendations with material tradeoffs, or consequential coverage/validation limits, if any.>

<One required-input question or the applicable Done gate.>
```

- Summarize in chat; omit empty fields and routine passing-check summaries. Use a short numbered list only for independent unresolved issues. Provide the complete finding disposition on request.

**Embedded command instructions**

Each section below applies only to its named review or implementation phase.

### review-clarity

<!-- Source: commands/review-clarity.md; sha256: 9f52d3860dfd05cbd5614447719230490d3e8a8121a1eeb0e789443f330f7951 -->

Review only — identify unclear names, misleading or redundant comments, and declarations placed far from use. No edits or fixes.

**Input:** The diff, paths, or symbols named in the message.

**Rules**

- Ask at most one question if the target is unclear; do not assume a target from earlier work
- Inspect the supplied scope and minimal surrounding context; for a diff, report findings on changed lines only
- Read-only — no file writes, Git mutations, or posted comments
- Judge names at their call sites: flag ambiguity, misleading meaning, or redundant context; follow language and repository conventions
- Check comments against behavior; retain explanations of intent, constraints, safety, and public contracts, and flag comments that merely repeat obvious code or mislead the reader
- Recommend narrower declaration scope or placement closer to use only when it improves understanding and preserves lifecycle and sharing requirements
- Identify the specific misunderstanding avoided; skip cosmetic preferences, wholesale renaming, and structural refactoring
- Before replying: verify each location and its surrounding usage; drop speculative findings and state any inspection limits

### review-duplication

<!-- Source: commands/review-duplication.md; sha256: 1507c020c7b3e26fc9e8b9849ecee4b325ac451ae8d2627c6096b51c725a5b44 -->

Review only — identify repeated implementation of the same rule that is worth sharing. No edits or fixes.

**Input:** The diff, paths, or symbols named in the message.

**Rules**

- Ask at most one question if the target is unclear; do not assume a target from earlier work
- Inspect the supplied scope and relevant counterparts or existing utilities; for a diff, anchor each finding on a changed line
- Read-only — no file writes, Git mutations, or posted comments
- Compare meaning, inputs, outputs, errors, and side effects; similar-looking code alone is not duplication worth removing
- Prefer an existing suitable utility; otherwise recommend the smallest shared helper or loop only when reduced maintenance outweighs added abstraction
- Preserve checks at distinct safety boundaries or against different object versions; do not merge checks with different failure meanings
- Cite the repeated locations and identify the shared rule; avoid generic frameworks or callbacks merely to save a few lines
- Review implementation duplication only; duplicate test-case coverage belongs to the existing review-test-cases command
- Before replying: confirm each finding represents the same rule and a concrete reuse benefit; drop speculative findings and state any inspection limits

### review-hardcoding

<!-- Source: commands/review-hardcoding.md; sha256: 16610a59e0b5fdf7b25264f205e7bb18619476608df5851670f0ac09dc1d4e2d -->

Review only — identify hardcoded values and field names with safer existing constants or typed alternatives. No edits or fixes.

**Input:** The diff, paths, or symbols named in the message.

**Rules**

- Ask at most one question if the target is unclear; do not assume a target from earlier work
- Inspect the supplied scope and minimal surrounding context; for a diff, report findings on changed lines only
- Read-only — no file writes, Git mutations, or posted comments
- Check stdlib, installed dependencies, and existing project definitions for constants, enums, or typed objects that express the same meaning
- Verify the replacement exists in the version used and preserves behavior, including serialization and omitted fields
- Recommend a new named constant only when it clarifies a meaningful domain value or centralizes a shared rule; do not extract every literal or make fixed values configurable without a requirement
- Report only concrete maintenance or correctness benefits; skip incidental literals and unrelated cleanup
- Before replying: verify each location and replacement; drop speculative findings and state any inspection limits

### review-redundancy

<!-- Source: commands/review-redundancy.md; sha256: c50aa3f7bed38fa2b014e2e713ef78afa12aec2ae958218a2f30cb5da639d291 -->

Review only — identify code, tests, documentation, and metadata references that serve no justified role in the intended delivery. No edits or fixes.

**Input:** A diff, feature, paths, or artifacts supplied in this turn; optional delivery baseline and supported deployments.

**Rules**

- Ask at most one initial question if the target is unclear; otherwise inspect the supplied scope and relevant requirements, callers, tests, references, and release evidence
- Read-only — no file writes, Git mutations, posted comments, or requirement changes
- Establish the reviewed revision or working-tree state and intended deliverables; distinguish tracked, untracked, and excluded artifacts. File presence does not establish delivery intent
- Separate development code, merged code, released behavior, and supported deployments; commits, implementation phases, and review PRs do not establish independently deployed versions or compatibility obligations
- Check migration paths, compatibility branches, fallbacks, abstractions, configuration, and supporting tests for dependencies on discarded designs or unsupported scenarios; distinguish necessary source adaptation from deployment migration
- Require evidence of a supported consumer, persisted state, or explicit compatibility obligation before treating an earlier design as a migration source. Never shipped does not by itself prove that no supported development deployment or data needs preservation
- Check documentation for obsolete procedures, repeated guidance, unsupported status claims, and dependencies on excluded artifacts; distinguish current instructions from intentionally retained history
- Check task IDs, phase numbers, PR history, and planning links in code comments and product documentation for relevance to the intended reader; preserve useful public API/product references and provenance in planning or historical artifacts
- Trace each candidate to its actual purpose and dependencies; implementation or a design entry alone does not prove necessity, and missing evidence alone does not prove redundancy. Cite both sides when sources conflict
- Recommend the smallest removal or correction with a concrete maintenance or clarity benefit; moving useful content, reducing file count, or shortening code alone is not a benefit
- Preserve required behavior, security boundaries, data integrity, operational guidance, and contractual obligations; account for affected callers, tests, and incoming references before recommending removal
- Keep scope on unnecessary artifacts and changes in the actual delivery; do not substitute repeated-code extraction, behavior-preserving refactoring, cosmetic cleanup, or broader feature tradeoffs
- Before replying: verify each finding's location, evidence, removal consequence, and delivery relevance; distinguish confirmed findings from unresolved assumptions, disclose coverage gaps, and do not recommend deleting a whole artifact because one part is obsolete

### review-simplify

<!-- Source: commands/review-simplify.md; sha256: 7c7df2e2ad69cc4f1f420606cc926480e6e72347a5821cfe815df32f1935f9e1 -->

Review only — identify ways to make code easier to follow while preserving behavior. No edits or fixes.

**Input:** The diff, paths, or symbols named in the message.

**Rules**

- Ask at most one question if the target is unclear; do not assume a target from earlier work
- Inspect the supplied scope and minimal surrounding context; for a diff, report findings on changed lines only
- Read-only — no file writes, Git mutations, or posted comments
- Check unnecessary branches, nesting, intermediate state, wrappers, and indirection against actual callers and contracts

### review-test-cases

<!-- Source: commands/review-test-cases.md; sha256: f5e58f71d9758642f3d30eae6b61ddb3f07911d5eddc7a0082c600fbfc07125d -->

Review only — flag test cases that duplicate both the code branch and runtime concern of another case. No edits, commits, or fixes.

**Input:** The test function or file named in the message.

**Rules**

- Read the test and the code under test — no writes, no git mutations
- For each test case, identify: (1) the code branch it exercises, (2) the runtime concern it validates (e.g. nil safety, type assertion, default behavior, error path)
- A case is unique if it covers a distinct branch OR a distinct runtime concern — it need not cover both
- Flag a case only when it duplicates both the branch and the runtime concern of another case
- In the detailed report, cite each duplicating pair by case name
- Skip style, naming, and structure nits — scope is duplication only
- Before replying: confirm each flagged pair truly shares both branch and concern; drop uncertain flags; return all supported pairs to the parent
- Must not — edit files, apply fixes, refactor, or rewrite tests

### review-value

<!-- Source: commands/review-value.md; sha256: 29ec87413a8115a869fd7fc8b3f85d14844f2ba0a9b84e64cb34cf43d533c264 -->

Review only — assess whether each feature and subfeature is worth its complexity, and recommend the smallest scope that meets real requirements. No edits or implementation.

**Input:** A feature, code path, diff, or design document; optional goals, constraints, and acceptable tradeoffs supplied in this turn.

**Rules**

- Ask at most one initial question if the target is unclear; otherwise inspect the supplied scope and relevant requirements, design, callers, and tests
- Read-only — no file writes, Git mutations, posted comments, or requirement changes
- Review every in-scope feature and independently meaningful subfeature, including safeguards, fallback paths, compatibility, retries, caches, configuration, rollout logic, and supporting tests; do not stop at the most obvious example
- For each, identify the problem it solves, who needs it, the evidence that it matters, its implementation and ongoing cost, and what happens without it
- Distinguish confirmed requirements, inferred needs, and optional choices; implementation or a design entry alone does not prove necessity, and missing evidence does not prove a feature is unnecessary
- Check actual deployment, release, scale, compatibility, and operational constraints before justifying complexity; separate smaller review PRs from independently deployed releases
- Compare keeping the feature with a simpler alternative, deferring it, or dropping it; weigh benefits against code, tests, dependencies, operations, and maintenance already present or still needed
- Consider accepting an edge case or operational limitation when it meets the user's goals; state the concrete consequence and who bears it, without inventing likelihoods, savings, or performance claims
- Preserve necessary security, data integrity, and contractual outcomes; distinguish them from optional mechanisms. A requirement change may be recommended, but must not be presented as agreed without explicit user evidence
- Assess whether to keep, simplify, defer, or drop each item internally; report only supported recommendations to change. Do not invent changes or present unresolved assumptions as decisions
- For Defer, identify a concrete condition that would justify revisiting it; for Simplify or Drop, identify affected requirements and dependent behavior so the saving is not overstated
- Keep this review about necessity and tradeoffs; do not substitute naming, formatting, or behavior-preserving refactoring advice
- Before replying: ensure every in-scope feature and subfeature was assessed, recommendations trace to evidence and real needs, and every proposed reduction accounts for its downside; surface it immediately when it changes the decision; disclose any coverage gaps

### implement

<!-- Source: commands/implement.md; sha256: 94323b369611ab663779886ef910bd1cd8c5ced3b521cb31e32e305b9f4f70cf -->

Implement only — source code changes for one scoped task. No commits, push, amend, or PRs.

**Input**

| Source | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| Doc    | Path to a design or plan doc + optional phase number(s) or title |
| Direct | Concrete task — fix, small feature, localized change |

Read referenced docs from the repo; treat as the spec.

**Rules**

- Ask at most one clarifying question if scope is unclear; otherwise state your assumption and proceed
- Implementation context — read the selected task, linked design sections, matching implementation companion, and referenced shared constraints in `implementation/README.md`. Resolve task links across sibling `tasks/` and `implementation/` folders, preserving legacy layouts; `implementation/history.md` is archival. Load only relevant sections; companions are optional when the supplied spec is sufficient. Archived instructions are historical evidence, not current work.
- Document conflicts — stop and surface conflicts between task criteria, design contracts, and implementation notes; notes must not silently override agreed behavior or reopen historical work
- Scoped work — only what the doc or task specifies, plus environment repairs needed to implement or validate it; stop and explain if the spec is insufficient
- Explain the purpose — opening update and completion lead with the concrete problem and intended or achieved behavior in plain language; task IDs, symbols, and file lists are supporting detail. Use a brief before/after example when it makes the change clearer.
- Report only achieved benefits — distinguish this task's result from benefits requiring later work; name the remaining dependency when needed to understand the result. Do not imply a defect existed or performance improved without evidence.
- Progress updates — report meaningful findings, blockers, or changed scope briefly; omit routine edit-by-edit narration
- Follow applicable user/project rules (coding and test standards) and language/ecosystem conventions for files you will touch
- Product documentation — write source comments and user-facing guidance in terms of behavior, contracts, and rationale; keep internal delivery-phase/task IDs and planning-document references in planning artifacts, not product content
- Run lint/tests as you go; fix failures caused by your changes; stop and report unrelated product defects
- Environment issues — diagnose and fix setup, dependency, tooling, or configuration issues blocking implementation or validation; use the smallest necessary repair, rerun the blocked step, and continue. Respect permissions; report a blocker only when repair requires unavailable access, credentials, or a user decision, and continue independent work where possible. Include repairs and any remaining validation limits in completion output.
- Suggested branch — provide one kebab-case name only when requested
- Must not — commit, push, amend, or open/update a PR; modify architecture or plan docs; work outside the stated spec except for necessary environment repairs
- Before replying: changed files match the spec; diff reviewed for coding-standards compliance (duplication, naming, locality); validation completed and decision-changing failures disclosed; the reader can tell why the change matters and what it delivers now; return task results to the parent workflow; its final output and Done gate apply once
